color-contrast (light).note: Measured 2026-08-09, after the per-site token swaps. Three causes remain. (1) WCAG-exempt inactive controls axe cannot recognise, because `disabled` sits on a custom element: `<wr-btn disabled>` labels, `wr-calendar__day--out-of-month`, and the disabled switch / checkbox labels (those use `--wr-color-on-surface-muted` correctly; it just happens to equal the `medium` intent in the dark theme). (2) `wr-squircle--bordered` — an ARTEFACT, not a defect: the content background is painted by a `::before` pseudo-element, which no DOM background walker can see, so axe falls back to the host's background-color — the BORDER colour — and compares the intent against itself. The real pairing there is ink-on-white at ~5.9:1. (3) The swatch grid on /guides/tokens/colors, which labels every shade of a ramp with `{intent}-contrast`, a token calibrated for the base shade only.

color-contrast (dark).note: The same causes as the light entry, on the pages where the dark theme also lands under 4.5.

target-size (light).note: wr-carousel's pagination dots. Measured 8x8 CSS px with centres 14px apart (the active dot is 20x8). WCAG 2.5.8 wants 24x24 targets, or undersized ones whose 24px circles do not intersect; 14px centres fail both. Every fix changes how the component LOOKS — bigger dots, or ~24px centre spacing — so it is a design call, not a defect to patch quietly. The `touch-target` mixin does not help: it is gated on `@media (pointer: coarse)`, and 2.5.8 applies to every pointer.

target-size (dark).note: Same component and the same measurement as the light entry — the dots are not themed.
